title: A Public Website Built Around Real Needs

paragraphs.en: The town’s fifth attempt to create a public-service website began in a pharmacy, where an ambulance crew had stopped to collect supplies. Their practical complaints were revealing. A deaf resident could not use the telephone service; a teen helping his mom found every medical page difficult to navigate. A businessman wanted a preview of planned road closures, while an unemployed resident needed information about support. The designers finally accepted that an online service should begin with its users rather than its departments.
paragraphs.zh: 城镇第五次尝试建设公共服务网站，起点竟是在药房里：救护车团队正停下来取物资。他们提出的实际问题很有启发。一位失聪居民无法使用电话服务；帮助妈妈办事的少年觉得每个医疗页面都难以查找。一位商人想提前了解道路封闭计划，一位失业居民则需要援助信息。设计者终于认识到，线上服务应从用户出发，而不是从部门架构出发。

paragraphs.en: A clinician reviewed the health pages with the new journalism team. A sore throat, a rash, and a bruise did not belong under one frightening heading. The difference between a benign tumor and a malignant one could not be explained by a single alarming photo. Pages mentioning a scar, a bandage, a capsule, or calcium needed a clear purpose and a responsible source. One draft confused the appendix with a vein; another treated every germ as equally dangerous. Accuracy mattered more than the volume of content.
paragraphs.zh: 一位临床医生与新的新闻团队一起审查健康页面。喉咙痛、皮疹和瘀伤不该统一归在一个吓人的标题下面。良性肿瘤与恶性肿瘤的区别，也无法靠一张令人紧张的照片解释。提及疤痕、绷带、胶囊或钙的页面，必须有明确用途和可靠来源。一份草稿把阑尾与静脉混淆，另一份则把所有病菌都当成同样危险。准确性比内容数量重要。

paragraphs.en: The education section recruited a freshman who enjoyed math to check a frequently quoted statistic. He discovered that a headline promising to slash waiting time lacked supporting data. A psychiatrist advised the team not to use psychiatry as a casual label for unusual behavior or describe a mortal illness as contagious without evidence. The influenza page distinguished general information from individual assessment. A student volunteer would proofread each revision, but specialist review remained necessary where an error could endanger a reader.
paragraphs.zh: 教育栏目请来一位喜欢数学的大一学生，检查一项频繁引用的统计数据。他发现，宣称将大幅削减等待时间的标题缺乏数据支持。一位精神科医生建议，不要随意给异常行为贴上精神病学标签，也不要没有证据就把致命疾病说成有传染性。流感页面区分一般信息与个人病情评估。学生志愿者会校对每次修订，但对于可能危害读者的错误，专业审查仍不可少。

paragraphs.en: Technology could simplify the work without replacing judgment. The team could automate an appointment reminder and design a lightweight app for a smartphone, but neither measure fixed uncertain instructions. One official proposed a flashy cartoon of a worker using a jack; users preferred a readable utility map. They also wanted the park page to explain how wildlife depended on the local ecosystem. Furthermore, making services accessible required a plan for residents who had neither a suitable device nor a reliable connection.
paragraphs.zh: 技术可以简化工作，却不能代替判断。团队能够自动发送预约提醒，也能为智能手机设计轻量应用，但这些做法都无法修复含糊的说明。一位官员提议放上工人使用千斤顶的花哨卡通，用户却更喜欢清晰的公共设施地图。他们还希望公园页面解释，野生动物怎样依赖本地生态系统。此外，真正的可及性也要求照顾没有合适设备或稳定网络的居民。

paragraphs.en: At the launch, an independent referee from a civic group asked whether the workforce had enough time to maintain the service. The library was meant to be a haven for residents needing assistance, yet staff had received no extra training. Public demand and staff capacity had to be considered together, just as a clinic’s intake process had to match available appointments. Otherwise, an impressive launch could mar trust. The team chose a smaller, well-maintained service over a larger collection of promises. Before adding another function, managers would examine unanswered questions and abandoned applications, treating those records as evidence about the service rather than as proof that users had failed to understand it. Residents could report broken links and confusing wording, giving staff a practical way to improve the service continually.
paragraphs.zh: 上线时，市民团体的一位独立评审询问，工作人员是否有足够时间维护服务。图书馆原本应成为需要帮助的居民安心求助的地方，员工却没有得到额外培训。公众需求与人员能力必须一起考虑，就像诊所接收患者的流程要与预约容量匹配。否则，再漂亮的发布也可能损害信任。团队选择了规模较小但维护可靠的服务，而不是一大堆承诺。每增加一种功能之前，管理者都要检查未回答的问题和半途放弃的申请，把这些记录视为有关服务的证据，而不是用户不理解服务的证明。居民可以报告失效链接和令人困惑的措辞，让工作人员有实际办法持续改进服务。
